text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Baltic presidents met NATO member delegations and the presidents of the three new member countries. President Meri invited President Clinton to visit Tallinn.
- New five and 10-kroon banknotes with improved security features will be introduced.
- The security police has initiated a case concerning the 1940 Soviet-promoted coup.
- Estonia hopes to receive an invite to join NATO in two years, Meri said in Madrid.
- The popular coastal town of Parnu has been overwhelmed by holidaymakers' cars and the local police have had to stop traffic going down some streets.
- An Estonian-written computer virus was detected in the World Bank computers on June 6 but no harm was done.
- The Geneva convention on refugees came into force.
- Privatisation vouchers went up at the stock exchange to an all-time high. Some traders suspect inside information to be the reason.
- Estonian and Russian law enforcement will continue cooperation via Interpol without the Soviet-era special communications line, the interior ministry announced.
